title: Integrating evolutionary and compositional features with ML and DL for robust and interpretable druggable protein prediction
abstract: Druggable proteins are essential targets in contemporary therapeutic discovery, and their precise identification is necessary for the progression of rational drug design. Traditional biochemical screening techniques are costly, laborious, and protracted, whereas current computational models typically attain only moderate efficacy and seldom offer robust statistical validation or biological interpretability. To mitigate these limitations, we offer a hybrid computational approach that integrates evolutionary and compositional information by merging Average Block-based Position-Specific Scoring Matrix (AB-PSSM) characteristics with Dipeptide Composition (DPC) into a 600-dimensional representation. The hybrid feature space was assessed utilizing three machine learning algorithms (support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) alongside three deep learning architectures (CapsBiLSTM, ResCapsNetPlus, and ResNet1D) following a rigorous five-fold out-of-fold cross-validation protocol to guarantee fairness and reproducibility. A thorough assessment revealed that the hybrid attributes significantly surpassed individual descriptors, with the SVM and CapsBiLSTM classifiers attaining classification accuracies of 90% and ROC-AUC and PR-AUC values surpassing 95%. By integrating complementary evolutionary and compositional descriptors within a rigorously controlled out-of-fold validation framework, the proposed method improves predictive stability compared with previously reported sequence-based and ensemble learning predictors. Furthermore, unlike many existing approaches that primarily rely on accuracy-based evaluation, this study incorporates statistical significance testing and interpretable feature attribution, enabling both reliable generalization performance and biological interpretability. The robustness and reliability were further validated by statistical analyses, including DeLong's test, McNemar's test, and bootstrap confidence intervals, demonstrating that the observed enhancements were substantial and consistent. Furthermore, interpretability investigations employing SHAP feature attribution and t-SNE visualization underscored biologically significant sequence descriptors as pivotal factors influencing druggability, thus mitigating the "black box" constraint inherent in numerous deep learning methodologies. This study presents a statistically validated, interpretable, and high-performing framework for predicting druggable proteins, demonstrating competitive performance compared with existing machine learning and ensemble-based predictors while providing improved statistical reliability and interpretability, thereby establishing a clear basis for future applications in precision medicine and drug discovery.

title: sorbaMOF DB: An Extensible MOF Adsorption Database Platform with a Case Study on Direct Air Capture of CO2
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into materials discovery is increasingly constrained by the quality and reliability of underlying datasets. This challenge is particularly critical for adsorption in Metal–Organic Frameworks (MOFs), where structural inconsistencies in widely used databases and the choice of force fields and charge models can strongly affect the reliability of predicted adsorption properties. Here, we introduce sorbaMOF DB, a general and extensible reliable MOF adsorption database.

title: Mechanism of C–H Activation/Amination by Paddle-Wheel Diruthenium Catalyst: Multireference Insight and Comparison with Dirhodium
abstract: Highly accurate multireference electronic-structure calculations elucidated the detailed mechanism of paddle-wheel dinuclear Ru-catalyzed C–H activation/amination. The reaction proceeds through a stepwise pathway consisting of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) from the allylic carbon to the nitrene nitrogen, followed by C–N bond formation. Multireference descriptions uncovered significant radical contributions in the nitrenoid intermediate, rationalizing the HAT character of the C–H activation step.

title: Staphylococcus FtsZ interfaces targeted by membrane-permeable BoltzGen cyclic-minipeptides
abstract: BoltzGen, Prodigy, Cyclops and PyMol/Python combinations computationally predicted permeable cyclic-minipeptides targeting intracellular cell-division FtsZ filaments of Staphylococcus aureus, one of the most important antibiotic-resistant Gram-positive bacterial human pathogens. In particular, this work targeted a downsized-FtsZαß dimer-interface model with cyclic-minipeptides. Except rank621, however all predicted cyclic-minipeptide membrane-permeabilities were low, despite their picoMolar affinities tops.

title: MOFEvolve: Literature-Driven Evolution of Experimental MOFs
abstract: The discovery of functional metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) requires computational workflows that can rapidly convert newly reported experimental knowledge into actionable design hypotheses. However, existing MOF discovery pipelines often rely on static structure databases and do not fully utilize the design rationale described in experimental literature. Here, we present MOFEvolve, an automated framework for literature-driven derivative design of experimental MOFs.

title: Synthesis of C2-SF4-Indoles in presence of Blue LED.
abstract: The increasing demand for fluorinated motifs beyond conventional PFAS-related CF3 and CF2 groups has stimulated interest in sulfur–fluorine-based alternatives. Herein, we report a blue LED-promoted one-pot synthesis of previously unknown Ar-SF4-linked indoles through a radical addition/cyclization sequence using aryl(heteroaryl)-SF4Cl reagents and N-(2-ethynylphenyl)sulfonamides. The method provides efficient access to a variety of pyridyl- and aryl-SF4-containing indoles under mild conditions.

title: Mineral-controlled heat-stiffening in dynamically crosslinked polymer networks
abstract: Dynamically crosslinked polymer networks are an important class of soft matter increasingly applied in several fields ranging from wearable electronics to biomedical applications in large part due to their useful stimuli-responsive behavior. However, these materials typically soften with increasing temperatures. Here we report a series of dynamically crosslinked mineral-polymer networks that exhibit a rare phenomenon of reversible heat-induced stiffening.

title: Artificial intelligence-empowered biochar engineering: From design fundamentals to commercialization
abstract: Engineered biochar is a promising carbon material for sustainable energy and environmental applications, yet its transition from laboratory-scale synthesis to commercial deployment remains constrained. Current developments largely relies on trial-and-error and heuristics-based approaches, making it difficult to establish synthesis-structure-performance relationships and posing reproducibility challenges across scales and locations. Recent years we have witnessed the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to navigate this complex design space.

title: From Fluorine to Iodine: Halogen Effects on Fluorescein Emission
abstract: Despite the fact that fluorescein probes are widely used in clinical diagnostics, including ophthalmology and gastrointestinal endoscopy, they continue to attract considerable scientific interest across diverse research areas, from fluorescein‑based voltage indicators and fluorogenic cancer biomarkers to modern organic photoredox catalysis. Although the effects of fluorination on fluorescein and the heavy‑atom influence on its emission properties have been examined separately in numerous studies, here we systematically investigate the complete fluorine‑to‑iodine substitution series within a…

title: Linker-Linker Coupling and Charge Storage Drive CO2 Photoreduction in Porphyrinic Zr(IV)-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing photoactive organic linkers are promising platforms for artificial photosynthesis, yet the nature of the photoactive state in Zr(IV)-based MOFs remains controversial, particularly the proposed involvement of transient Zr(III) centers formed through linker-to-node charge transfer. Here, we elucidate the mechanism of CO 2 -to-formate conversion in MOFs by comparing redox-active PCN-223 with redox-inactive UiO-66-NH 2 .

title: Importance may not be that important: A common misconception in data-driven materials development
abstract: With the growing adoption of machine learning methods in physics, data-driven materials development has emerged as one of the most prominent methodologies in materials research. In data-driven materials development, feature importance is often misused to infer direct relationships between input descriptors and material properties, because importance merely reflects a feature’s contribution to reducing model error, rather than its physical significance.

title: Diffusion and transport of hydrogen peroxide across lipid membranes
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important biological oxidant that can be formed both enzymatically and non-enzymatically, and several enzymatic systems are capable of rapidly decomposing it. During its short lifetime, H 2 O 2 can participate in cell signaling at low concentrations or induce irreparable molecular damage at high concentrations. The diffusion of H 2 O 2 in cells and tissues remains under debate, particularly regarding the role of cellular membranes as barriers to its diffusion and the mechanisms involved in its transport.

title: Spatial Heterogeneity of the Fluorine-to-Lithium Ratio as a Descriptor of Battery Failure by Laser-Induced XUV Spectroscopy (LIXS)
abstract: Fluorine-containing phases are closely linked to electrolyte decomposition, interphase formation, and failure processes in Li-ion batteries, yet their spatially resolved analysis in composite cathodes remains difficult. Here, laser-induced XUV spectroscopy (LIXS) was used to map fluorine- and lithium-related emission lines in composite lithium cobalt oxide cathodes (LCO). The study used the fluorine emission line at λ = 12.72 nm and the lithium emission line at λ = 13.42 nm and applied them to pristine, formed, aged, and failed LCO cathodes.

title: High-throughput site scoring of SNAr electrophiles using graph-local xTB/Fukui descriptors
abstract: Nucleophilic aromatic substitution (S N Ar) is widely used to functionalize electron-poor aryl and heteroaryl halides, but quantitative prediction of reaction barriers and site selectivity becomes more challenging when several C–X bonds can react. A semiempirical site-scoring equation was developed for the 74-substrate benzyl alcohol/DMSO benchmark reported by Lu–Paci–Leitch. The model uses xTB-derived global reactivity descriptors and atom-condensed Fukui indices evaluated in a graph-local environment around each candidate aromatic C–X bond.

title: Accelerating and Scaling On-Lattice Solid-on-Solid Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations Using an Autoregressive Conditional Variational Autoencoder
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations are fundamental for modeling atomistic surface morphology evolution, but their inherently sequential execution of atomic steps creates severe computational bottlenecks. This computational burden restricts accessible time-and length scales, making dynamic coupling with continuum solvers, such as Computational Fluid Dynamics, difficult. To overcome these limitations, this work introduces a novel surrogate model based on an autoregressive fully convolutional Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE).

title: Freestanding van der Waals C60 Thin Films
abstract: Freestanding thin films have enabled the study of intrinsic material properties by eliminating substrate-induced constraints, yet their preparation has been limited to covalently bonded or strongly interconnected materials. Molecular solid thin films, stabilized by weak van der Waals (vdW) interactions, remain largely unexplored in freestanding form due to their inherent mechanical instability. Here, we establish a simple sublimation-assisted strategy to fabricate freestanding films of fullerene C60 as a model molecular solid.

title: Noble Gas Aggregation and Dynamics in Molten Alkali Chloride Salts
abstract: Noble gas behavior in molten alkali chloride salts is important for understanding gas retention, transport, and removal in high-temperature molten salt environments. Although previous molecular simulations have examined single-particle properties such as noble gas solubility and diffusion, the thermodynamics of early-stage gas aggregation in molten salts remain less well understood. Here, we develop an ab initio-informed classical molecular dynamics framework for quantifying stepwise noble gas aggregation in molten LiCl and KCl.

title: Transitioning from glassware to plasticware in an industrial analytical laboratory following a laceration incident : A case study
abstract: Glassware-related lacerations are the most frequent category of injury in chemistry laboratories. Despite this, manual dishwashing, a daily routine step in every analytical laboratory, is virtually absent from safety literature as a distinct risk context. Here, we report a case study from an incident at the quality control laboratory of Saipol (Groupe Avril), a major European oilseed processing company, where a laboratory technician sustained a hand laceration requiring three sutures following the breakage of a glass beaker during post-analytical rinsing.

title: Flame Spray Pyrolysis Tailored In2O3-ZrO2 Hetero-Contacts for Enhanced Hydrogen Production in DME Steam Reforming
abstract: Dimethyl ether steam reforming (SRD) is a promising route for efficient, on-demand hydrogen generation. In2O3-ZrO2 has proven to be a promising catalyst, when physically mixed with γ-Al2O3 yet its activity relies strongly on the nature and density of oxide-oxide heterointerfaces. Here, we use single- and double-flame spray pyrolysis (S-FSP, DFSP) to tune the hetero-contacts of In2O3-ZrO2 catalysts. Across indium loadings (1-15 wt%), D-FSP consistently outperforms S-FSP, particularly at low reaction temperatures (325-350 °C) relevant for energy-efficient H2 release.

title: RETRACTED: Pulsed selectivity programming of photothermal CO2 hydrogenation
abstract: Retracted at the authors' request because a recently discovered experimental artefact renders the conclusions unreliable. Pulsed optical excitation is an emerging strategy to control heterogeneous catalysis beyond steady-state operation. Here, we compare photothermal CO₂ hydrogenation over Ru/SrTiO₃ under 1064 nm pulsed and continuous-wave illumination, without any auxiliary heat source.

title: Plasticize me sweetly: sugar-based plasticizers for poly(lactic acid)
abstract: Carbohydrates are among the most abundant biopolymers in the world and offer a promising source for the synthesis of value-added chemicals. Galactaric acid is an attractive bio-based building block that has not yet been fully exploited. Currently, regulatory, sustainability, safety-by-design and performance requirements for polymer additives are becoming increasingly strict. As a result, innovation in this field must be accelerated to develop new materials with enhanced properties. With this objective, new sugar-based plasticizers based on galactaric acid have been synthesised.

title: Accurate Molecular Properties via Bootstrap Embedding
abstract: We demonstrate the utility of back-transformed bootstrap embedding (BE) one- and two-particle density matrices (1 and 2-PDMs) by computing dipole moments and force gradients for several polar systems. The resulting mean absolute error in atomic force gradients at BE2/CCSD is approximately 0.003 au/bohr even in most polar and strained environments, and these forces further enable stable geometry optimization trajectories. We refer to this approach for generating molecular properties as Bootstrap Embedding-Direct Matrices (BE-DM).

title: Catalytic Desymmetrization Unlocks Enantioselective Access to Chiral Triptycene Scaffolds
abstract: Chiral triptycene frameworks with intrinsic three-dimensional rigidity constitute versatile building blocks for asymmetric catalysis and circularly polarized luminescence materials, yet catalytic highly enantioselective routes toward their asymmetric construction remain underexplored. Herein, we report an N -heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed desymmetrizing acylation of triptycenyl diphenols via acylative functionalization with diverse aldehydes, furnishing enantioenriched chiral triptycene derivatives.

title: A linear relationship linking the aggregated isotopic moments of a molecular formula to those of its constituent elements
abstract: It has long been recognized that the isotope patterns of unknown analytes provide valuable information that facilitates the determination of their molecular formulas in mass spectrometry experiments. It is primarily the combined abundances of isotopic variants aggregated by the number of nucleons, as well as the associated aggregated masses that have been used for this purpose. However, there is additional information in the higher moments or alternatively in the higher cumulants of the aggregated isotope patterns, which is rarely exploited.

title: Prioritizing early opportunities to enhance carbon efficiency at biorefineries
abstract: Biorefineries are a critical component of society’s transition from fossil-derived to bio-derived fuel and chemical production, but their life cycle carbon efficiency is often undermined by the underutilization of biomass feedstocks during processing. In this work, we explore the feasibility and sustainability implications of integrating waste carbon utilization into commercial-scale biorefineries through process design, simulation, techno-economic analysis, and life cycle assessment under uncertainty.

title: High-throughput synthesis and screening of cyclometallated iridium complexes for antibacterial applications
abstract: The discovery of novel antibiotics to address the rise of antimicrobial resistance is an increasingly pressing issue for global health. In recent years transition metal complexes have gained attention as potential antibacterial agents. We herein describe a new methodology to generate hundreds of novel cyclometallated iridium compounds with bidentate Schiff ligands in a high-throughput combinatorial approach, alongside the expansion of an existing approach using bidentate pyridine-triazole ligands, with the aim of finding new metalloantibiotics.

title: Isobutanol Dehydration to Linear Butenes on Ferrierite: Mechanistic Insights from operando FTIR, Chemometrics and Kinetic Modelling
abstract: The selective dehydration of isobutanol to linear butenes catalyzed by acidic ferrierite (H-FER) has been investigated by operando IR spectroscopy under close batch conditions and along a temperature ramp. The employed apparatus permits to alternatively acquire spectra of both the gas phase composition and the species adsorbed on the H-FER surface, thus providing fundamental insights onto the products formation and the reaction intermediates formed on the catalyst surface.

title: Skeletal editing as synthetic tool to prepare benzo[e][1,2,4]triazines from 2aminobenzimidazoles via nitrogen atom insertion
abstract: Herein, we report a one-pot, two-step reaction that converts readily available 2-aminobenzimidazoles into scarcely accessible benzo[e][1,2,4]triazines via nitrogen atom insertion. This sequential transformation includes an electrophilic amination step with bench-stable MSH.HOTf, followed by an oxidation with commercial hypervalent iodine reactant. The developed reaction encompasses a wide array of functional handles that could be exploited for post-modification, thus highlighting the synthetic utility of the present work.

title: Accelerated Stable Structure Prediction of Li-Intercalated Bilayer Graphene Using a Data-Efficient Deep Learning Framework
A Critical Evaluation of Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Organic Synthesis: Activation Modes and Green Metrics
abstract: While domino and cascade reactions are widely celebrated for their step economy and intrinsic bond-forming efficiency, evaluating their true sustainability requires moving beyond a purely molecular perspective to incorporate rigorous Green Chemistry metrics. This review critically reassesses sequential transformations—including ionic, radical, pericyclic, photochemical, transition-metal, and biocatalytic pathwaysthrough a quantitative framework termed the “Molecular–Process Discrepancy.” Rather than providing a traditional descriptive overview, this manuscript integrates quantitative…

title: Polypyrrole-Polydopamine Composite Conductive Polymers for Electrical Stimulation in Tissue Engineering
abstract: Conductive polymers have emerged as a paramount category of biomaterials within the domains of tissue engineering and regenerative medicine, attributed to their capacity for transmitting electrical signals and facilitating effective interactions with cellular entities. Among this class of materials, polypyrrole (PPy) has been extensively utilized in the development of electroactive scaffolds, systems for cellular stimulation, and bioelectronic interfaces, owing to its advantageous electrical conductivity and commendable biocompatibility.

title: CoSyER: A high-throughput data generation approach for environmental machine learning
abstract: Machine learning holds great promise for chemical hazard assessment, but the lack of large, standardized datasets limits advances. We herein propose Co mbinatorial Sy nthesis for E nvironmental R esearch ( CoSyER ) as a high-throughput data generation approach for environmental machine learning, capable of generating hazard data for hundreds of compounds within weeks. To demonstrate proof of concept, we synthesized ~300 organophosphate ester (OPE) mixture via one-pot combinatorial synthesis.

title: Exploring the Chemical Space with a Foundation Model for Optimizing Drug Discovery in Neglected Diseases, the case of Leishmaniasis
abstract: Applications of AI to the discovery of new treatments could have a large impact on the acceleration of drug discovery for neglected diseases such as Leishmaniasis. Taking advantage of a lead compound derived from a library of 1.8 million molecules screened against Leishmaniasis Infantum and a dataset used for further refining the lead compound potency and metabolic stability, we fine-tuned a foundational model MMELON (Multi-view Molecular Embedding with Late Fusion) to accurately predict these properties with high AUROCs of 0.90 and 0.87 respectively.

title: Laser-directed photochemical synthesis of complex DNA microarrays and libraries
abstract: In situ photolithographic synthesis of nucleic acids offers high-throughput capability and versatility across a wide range of canonical and analog nucleic acid chemistries, substrates, and surface functionalization strategies. However, adapting this synthetic approach to new applications involving physically large layouts and dispersed or larger features requires an optical exposure system capable of delivering light with greater flexibility than that offered by digital micromirror device technology.

title: Mechanism of Zwitterionic Photochromism in Aza-Diarylethenes Revealed by Direct Observation of a Closed-Ring Intermediate
abstract: Aza-diarylethenes have emerged as a unique class of photochromic molecules exhibiting reaction pathways that are inaccessible to conventional diarylethenes. In particular, certain azadiarylethenes generate zwitterionic closed-ring photoproducts, giving rise to unusual photochromic behavior. However, the elementary processes responsible for the formation of zwitterionic photoproducts remain unclear, hindering mechanistic understanding of this unusual class of photochromic reactions.

title: Recent advances in cis/trans stereoselective polymerizations toward functional materials with tailored properties
abstract: Despite the myriad of stereoselective reactions developed to control the cis/trans (or Z/E) configuration of alkenes, analogous stereocontrol has been slower to emerge in polymerization processes. Following pioneering work in stereoselective coordination–insertion polymerizations, a variety of cis/trans stereoselective processes have recently been reported, enabling the synthesis of well-defined polymeric materials with tunable properties.

title: Electrochemical Cu-ion Insertion in a Tunnel-Structured V2O5 Polymorph
abstract: The distinctive nonlinear dynamical transitions of “neuromorphic” inorganic materials provide a means to build spiking oscillatory circuits for brain-inspired computing. The metal-insulator transition of β′-Cu x V 2 O 5 is controlled by the Cu stoichiometry. Electrochemical Cu-ion insertion into the empty metastable ζ-V 2 O 5 polymorph utilizing an aqueous electrolyte is demonstrated for the first time. X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy techniques in combination with electron microscopy elucidate electronic and structural evolution as a function of Cu-ion insertion.

title: Hetero-interfacial Oxygen superionic conduction for efficient high-temperature CO2 Electrolysis
abstract: Solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) hold enormous potential for the conversion of CO2 into high-value fuels, yet their performance is often limited by insufficient oxygen‑ion conductivity and sluggish CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) kinetics. Herein, we develop a hetero-interface superionic conductor that integrates cross-grain bridging and the space charge effect to boost CO2 electrolysis performance of double perovskite electrodes.

title: Approach-Region Commitment and Environmental Friction
abstract: The commitment of a reacting system to productive barrier crossing depends on how strongly the environment dissipates energy into the approach-region coordinate, rather than oscillatory recrossing. This dissipation is quantified by a single dimensionless damping ratio, χ0 = Γeff/(2Ω0), where Ω0 is the precursor-well approach frequency and Γeff is the total projected friction.

title: Quantum-Guided Binding-Site Engineering of Lanmodulin for Zero-Waste Separation of Critical Rare-Earth Elements
abstract: Rare-earth separation remains energy-intensive and waste-generating, motivating aqueous alternatives for selective lanthanide capture. We report a deterministic computational workflow that couples binding-site engineering of lanmodulin with multireference quantum characterization toward dysprosium prioritization. Four experimentally solved lanmodulin structures were harmonized, residue roles were assigned to preserve the first-shell coordination environment while allowing selected second-sphere and interface positions to mutate, and ProteinMPNN, LigandMPNN, Rosetta triage, and reduced OpenMM…

title: Active Space Compression High Fidelity Variational Solvers and Exact Consistency under Quantum Molecular Mechanics Embedding
abstract: This study presents a journal ready quantum molecular simulation paper built around a reproducible workflow that couples active space reduction, variational quantum solvers, and simple QM MM electrostatic embedding for benchmark molecules relevant to chemical and biological modeling. The central challenge addressed is the mismatch between realistic molecular Hamiltonians and near term qubit limits. We hypothesized that disciplined active space compression would preserve energy fidelity while transforming otherwise impractical problems into compact qubit representations.

title: Radiosynthesis and PET/CT evaluation of 18F-labeled and non-steroidal androgen receptor inhibitor, [18F]F -ARi, in a non-castrated model
abstract: Androgen receptor (AR)-targeted positron emission tomography (PET) enables non-invasive quantification of AR expression in androgen driven prostate cancer cases. The clinically investigated tracer 16β-[ 18 F]F-fluorodihydrotestosterone ([ 18 F]F-DHT) is limited by endogenous androgen competition in non-castrated patients, rapid metabolism and restricted bioavailability. To address these limitations, we developed a non-steroidal AR-targeted radiotracer, [ 18 F]F-ARi, derived from the precursor ARi-NH, for AR-targeted PET imaging.

title: Computational Design of Two Selective Tyrosine Kinase 2 Inhibitors
abstract: Dysregulated interleukin-12 (IL-12) and interleukin-23 (IL-23) cytokine signaling pathways have been implicated in many inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease, plaque psoriasis, or rheumatoid arthritis. While small molecule or biologic therapies exist to target IL-12 and IL-23, limitations to selectivity or long-term efficacy reflect a need for novel drug candidates. Tyrosine Kinase 2 (TYK2), one of four Janus Kinase enzymes, is involved in intracellular IL-12 and IL-23 signal transduction and has been of recent pharmacological interest.

title: Alkylthio aurone fluorophores: a structure–property relationship of emission in solution and in the solid state
abstract: Aurones are a class of fluorescent plant flavonoids representing biocompatible fluorophores with tuneable emission colors. In this work, a series of novel 4'-alkylthio aurones is synthesized and their steady-state and time-resolved emission is studied in solution- and solid state in combination with the single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. In solution, the aurones possess virtually identical cyan fluorescence with similar parameters.

title: OSC700: A GW+BSE Dataset of 700 Organic Semiconductor (OSC) Crystals with an LLM-Assisted Data Extraction Agent
abstract: Key parameters for organic optoelectronic device applications derive from the excited-state properties of molecular crystals. Data scarcity (both experimental and theoretical) limits the ability to train machine learning (ML) models to predict these properties. We present the OSC700 dataset of excited-state properties of 700 crystalline organic semiconductors (OSCs) with up to 1168 atoms in the unit cell, calculated using state-of-the-art many-body perturbation theory within the GW approximation and Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW+BSE).

Integration of transcriptomic data reveals lipid metabolic heterogeneity and identifies GSTO1 as a therapeutic target in acute myeloid leukemia
abstract: BackgroundAcute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy with poor prognosis and significant heterogeneity. Lipid metabolic reprogramming is a key hallmark of cancer, yet its systemic characterization and clinical relevance in AML remain largely unexplored.MethodsMulti-omics data were integrated, including one single-cell RNA-seq dataset and bulk transcriptomes from nine AML cohorts. Lipid metabolism activity was assessed using GSVA. Consensus clustering based on lipid metabolism pathways identified molecular subtypes. A lipid metabolism-related prognostic signature (LMRS) was constructed via machine learning algorithms and validated across nine independent cohorts. Functional validation was performed in AML cell lines using GSTO1 inhibition.ResultsSingle-cell analysis revealed significant upregulation of lipid metabolism pathways in AML malignant cells, particularly in progenitor-like subpopulations. Three lipid metabolism-based subtypes (C1-C3) were identified, with the C3 subtype exhibiting the highest metabolic activity, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and the worst prognosis. A robust nine-gene LMRS model was developed, which effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct survival outcomes. LMRS demonstrated superior predictive accuracy over existing models, was independently prognostic, and correlated with chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance. Inhibition of GSTO1 significantly induced apoptosis and ROS production in AML cells.ConclusionThis study comprehensively defines lipid metabolic heterogeneity in AML, establishes a clinically applicable prognostic signature, and underscores lipid metabolism as a key driver of AML progression and immunosuppression. Targeting lipid metabolism, particularly through GSTO1 inhibition, represents a promising therapeutic strategy.
